scope: Selective publisher/proceedings citations, not a systematic literature review.

adaptiveAR.title: Designing adaptive feedback systems for managing cognitive load in augmented reality
adaptiveAR.scope: Existing adaptive physiological feedback in AR means adapting an interface is not by itself a novel contribution.

adaptiveVR.title: Towards Intelligent VR Training: A Physiological Adaptation Framework for Cognitive Load and Stress Detection
adaptiveVR.scope: Physiology-driven VR adaptation has been demonstrated; independent behavioural gains require direct controlled trials.

smartAR.title: Adaptive interaction in intelligent augmented reality: design decision considerations and framework
smartAR.scope: A recent synthesis already maps adaptation and interaction choices; the proposed new result must specify a narrow causal estimand.

metaCL.title: Can augmented reality technology reduce learners' cognitive load? A meta-analysis
metaCL.scope: Average reductions in learning load do not establish gains from the particular adaptive controller in a new scene.

ground.title: SeeGround: See and Ground for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary 3D Visual Grounding
ground.scope: 3D grounding with VLM is prior art; the new study must demonstrate calibrated AR anchor gains, not merely combining 2D and 3D.

words.title: Words into World: A Task-Adaptive Agent for Language-Guided Spatial Retrieval in AR
words.scope: Task-adaptive spatial language retrieval and meter-accurate anchors are already proposed, narrowing independent novelty.

assembly.title: Evaluation of augmented reality instructions based on initial and dynamic assembly tolerance allocation schemes in precise manual assembly
assembly.scope: AR assistance for precise manual procedures is established; independent sequential error detection requires a different endpoint.

manual.title: Deep learning-based augmented reality work instruction assistance system for complex manual assembly
manual.scope: AI-generated AR work instructions are prior art; measure the specific temporal error/omission mechanism.

proactive.title: Sensible Agent: A Framework for Unobtrusive Interaction with Proactive AR Agents
proactive.scope: Proactive LMM-based AR assistance exists; evaluate the behavioural difference under a fixed number of interventions.

eye.title: Validity of Eye-Tracking Measures in Immersive Virtual Reality: Using Cognitive Theories of Learning
eye.scope: Eye tracking in immersive VR requires explicit validity and construct assumptions; device integration cannot be presumed.

eeg.title: The integration of virtual reality and EEG: A step-by-step guideline
eeg.scope: EEG/VR time alignment and experimental validity must be explicitly documented before any multimodal inference claim.

timing.title: The Art of Timing: Effects of AR Guidance Timing on Speed Control
timing.scope: AR guidance timing has already been manipulated experimentally; novelty needs phase-specific step errors, not generic scheduling.

hands.title: Exploring AR hand augmentations as error feedback mechanisms for enhancing gesture-based tutorials
hands.scope: Prior hand-gesture AR guidance has tested error feedback; establish a distinct motor-phase or procedural endpoint.

social.title: Creating a social virtual reality application for psychological research: A tutorial
social.scope: Multiuser VR research protocols exist, so interaction-format effects must be isolated under controlled social and scene conditions.

trust.title: An Investigation of Trust and Overreliance on Conversational Instructions in Augmented Reality
trust.scope: Human reliance on AR-provided AI instructions is already studied; measuring trust alone does not establish correct guidance.

training.title: Can augmented reality technology reduce learners' cognitive load? A meta-analysis
training.scope: Learning-load effects do not imply delayed knowledge retention or skill transfer.

VRET.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) for virtual reality exposure therapy (VRET): A systematic review
VRET.scope: AI adaptation in exposure contexts already exists; this plan is not a treatment efficacy study and requires dedicated clinical review.

personal.title: Adapting to the User: A Systematic Review of Personalized Interaction in VR
personal.scope: XR personalization methods exist; a claim needs a defined multi-session or transfer contrast.

perspect.title: Comparison of visual and multisensory augmented reality for precise manual manipulation tasks
perspect.scope: AR versus other guidance modalities is established; a new effect needs precise task and performance definitions.

EXAD.title: EXAD: Framework for Designing Explanations in Adaptive User Interfaces
EXAD.scope: Explanation design in adaptive interfaces is prior art; response to veridical versus spurious explanations needs separate evaluation.
